chunks: And al-Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — also informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Maysara, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, whether the recitation of poetry invalidates wudu. He said: «No».
As for al-madhy (pre-seminal fluid) and al-wadhy (post-urination drops), they do not invalidate wudu; and what indicates this [is as follows].

key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: al-madhy: pre-seminal fluid emitted without ejaculation; a classical jurisprudential category
key_terms.الْوَذْيُ: al-wadhy: thin fluid discharged after urination; a classical jurisprudential category

ai.seo_question: Does reciting poetry invalidate wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Mu'awiya ibn Maysara asked Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) whether the recitation of poetry (inshad al-shi'r) invalidates wudu; the Imam replied in the negative. The compiler al-Tusi then notes that al-madhy (pre-seminal fluid) and al-wadhy (post-urination drops) likewise do not invalidate wudu, introducing the evidentiary discussion that follows in the chapter.
